structured_output.what_is_happening: A 20-minute-old token called 'Apu', launched directly on PumpSwap (not from the pump.fun curve), has done $448k of volume on a $21k market cap. That is about 14.7x turnover in 20 minutes. Its price is up 108%. Another 'Apu' pump.fun coin (79xB…pump) was created about 12 minutes earlier and is already at a $905k market cap with $490k of hourly volume. This token is almost certainly a copycat riding that coin's attention. The flow data looks manufactured. There were 1,939 unique buyers but only 52 unique sellers. 1,200 of those buyers came in a single 15-minute window, but only 42 in the last 5 minutes. That pattern fits bot 'holder-farming' micro-buys plus a few wallets doing large sells. GMGN also flags 42 bundler wallets holding 16.6% of top-trader share. The creator has already closed their position ('creator_close'). The LP burn ratio is 0, and liquidity ($30.5k) is larger than market cap, so most of the supply sits in a pool the creator can pull.

narrative.description: Apu (Apu Apustaja / Pepe-adjacent meme) name spillover from a same-name pump.fun coin that is running hard right now at ~$905k mcap.
narrative.why_spreading: The attention belongs to the canonical Apu pump.fun coin. This copy gets spillover from people searching the ticker and from bots, not its own story.

token_connection.why_this_token: Same name and ticker, launched about 12 minutes after the leading Apu coin, directly on PumpSwap with an unburned LP. That is a classic clone pattern.
token_connection.competing_tokens: 79xB7iLghccAWuoab7qXkaDpQggmu6D2zrpKtfXipump (Apu, $905k mcap, $490k h1 vol) is the clear leader. There are also several dead APU clones and older Apu Apustaja tokens, plus another fresh clone, Fqs6…pump.

authenticity.evidence: 1,939 unique buyers against 52 unique sellers. Buyers spiked to 1,200 in 15 minutes and fell to 42 in the last 5 minutes. 42 bundler wallets (16.6% of top-trader share). Turnover of 14.7x on a $21k market cap. No socials on DexScreener and only 41 GMGN page visits despite '1,940 holders'. That mismatch strongly suggests bot-inflated holder counts and volume.
authenticity.uncertainty: No X data. The Twitter handle TheApuPf exists but its content and reach are unknown. Some real spillover buyers from the leading Apu coin are likely.

structural_risks: LP burn ratio 0: the creator-created PumpSwap pool can be pulled
Liquidity larger than market cap: most of the supply sits in the pullable pool
Clone of a same-name runner, so attention can collapse when the leader fades
Buyer/seller asymmetry suggests fake holder counts

structured_output.counterargument: Mint and freeze authority are renounced, there are no taxes, and the top-10 holders own only 16%. Spillover from a leading Apu coin at about $1M could keep pushing buyers into cheap clones. At a $21k market cap, a 2x only needs $42k. If the creator's goal is volume farming rather than pulling liquidity, the price could keep grinding up for a while.

structured_output.thesis: This is a copycat Apu clone launched directly on PumpSwap with an unburned LP and a creator who has exited. Its activity looks bot-farmed (1,939 buyers against 52 sellers, 42 bundlers). The attention belongs to the leading Apu coin. The likely outcome is a liquidity pull or a slow bleed, not a 2x.
